sections.title: Numbers to a Hundred
sections.content: You have been reading prices since Lesson 8 and dates since Lesson 10. Here is the whole system. Learn one to fifteen, because they are their own words. From sixteen to twenty-nine Spanish writes the number as one word — dieciséis, veintidós. From thirty-one up it splits again, joined by 'y': treinta y uno, cuarenta y cinco.

sections.title: Sixteen and up
rows: treinta, treinta y uno, treinta y dos

sections.title: Things you count

items.spanish: Hay dos autobuses: el número doce y el número treinta.
items.english: There are two buses: the number twelve and the number thirty.

items.spanish: El doce va al centro. Son quince paradas.
items.english: The twelve goes to the centre. It's fifteen stops.

items.spanish: Tiene un billete de cincuenta mil y dos de diez mil.
items.english: She has a fifty-thousand note and two tens.

items.spanish: Dentro hay veintidós personas y solo dos asientos libres.
items.english: Inside there are twenty-two people and only two free seats.

sections.content: 'Uno' loses its o in front of a masculine noun: 'un billete', 'treinta y un minutos'. Before a feminine noun it becomes 'una': 'veintiuna personas'.
